summary: Strengthen NGO accounting, fund controls, and donor financial reporting in 5 days.
lede: NGO accounting and financial reporting training covers tracking restricted funds, controlling expenditure, and connecting grant activity with financial statements. It is for NGO finance managers, grant accountants, and programme finance officers who prepare donor and management reports. Participants practise designing a chart of accounts, reconciling bank and fund ledgers, analysing grant budgets against actuals, and preparing audit evidence, supported by COSO controls and Excel-based analysis.
audienceIntro: NGO financial reporting training suits professionals who prepare, review, approve, audit, or use financial information across grants, programmes, operations, and governance. Each role can adapt the exercises to its own accounting system and funding structure.
modules: NGO Accounting Foundations and Fund Structures
IPSAS and IFRS Financial Statement Preparation
Grant Accounting and Donor Budget Control
NGO Close, Reconciliations, and Audit Evidence
COSO Internal Controls for NGO Finance
Digital NGO Reporting and Financial Analytics
NGO Financial Strategy and Action Planning
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to bookkeeping, budgeting, grant administration, or financial reporting in an NGO or nonprofit setting. Working knowledge of debits, credits, spreadsheets, budgets, and basic financial statements is expected. No programming is required. Advanced digital topics are taught at operational application level, while Excel and Power BI exercises use guided templates rather than production-system configuration.
